title: Dependability cadence experiments and contacts (February 2027)
content:
Context:
This working doc captures a set of short-run experiments to validate a sustainable cross-team dependability cadence. The goal is to move from ad-hoc SLO policing to a predictable, collaborative rhythm that reduces firefighting, improves signal handoffs, and surfaces regressions earlier.

Why a cadence experiment?
- Too many distinct escalation patterns across teams; hard for SRE to maintain consistent risk posture.
- Alerts often fire without clear ownership or rollback path.
- Engineering teams want lightweight guarantees and clearer signals tied to product-level SLAs, not just infra metrics.

High-level objectives (90 days):
1) Define a repeatable weekly cadence for dependability reviews that fits existing sprint rhythms.
2) Validate 3 hypotheses via experiments that aim to lower P90 incident-to-ack latency and reduce noisy alerts by 30% in targeted services.
3) Produce a contact catalog and on-call handshake templates to be adopted by 6 product teams in the pilot.

Experiment matrix (run in parallel for 8 weeks):
- Experiment A: "Signal-to-Person mapping"
  Hypothesis: A one-page signal map (metric -> owner -> runbook link) reduces first-contact ambiguity and lowers ack time by >20%.
  Method: Work with two product teams; create signal maps for top-10 alerts; embed owners in paging rules.
  Success metric: Median ack time drops by 20% vs baseline.
  Owner: Miguel Rivera (ENG-4321)

- Experiment B: "Weekly dependability 30-min sync"
  Hypothesis: A short weekly sync between SRE, product leads, and infra reduces recurring postmortem themes and surfaces emerging capacity risks earlier.
  Method: Timeboxed 30-min slot, rotating facilitator, two agenda items: 'hot signals' and 'action quick wins'. Capture actions in a shared board.
  Success metric: Number of recurring postmortem action items related to missing signal decreases by 50% across pilot teams.
  Owner: Leah Wong

- Experiment C: "Shadowed on-call handoff"
  Hypothesis: A lightweight 48-hour shadowing pair (SRE + product on-call) reduces mis-routed escalations and improves cross-team blameless communication.
  Method: Schedule shadow windows for three teams; collect qualitative feedback and measure mis-routes.
  Success metric: Mis-routes (alerts routed to wrong team) reduced by 40% in pilot window.
  Owner: Connor Ellis

Deliverables (per experiment):
- One-page signal map (pdf & Confluence)
- Template: Oncall handshake email + Slack message + runbook link
- 30-day retrospective note with metrics and recommended next-step

Contact catalog (pilot):
- SRE lead (Dependability): Asha Patel - asha.patel@redwood.ai - primary coordinator
- SRE engineer (Signals): Miguel Rivera - miguel.rivera@redwood.ai - signal maps + alert tuning
- Product reliability partner (Search): Priya Desai - priya.desai@redwood.ai - pilot team A lead
- Product reliability partner (Embeddings): Connor Ellis - connor.ellis@redwood.ai - pilot team B lead
- Console/Telemetry owner: Leah Wong - leah.wong@redwood.ai - dashboards and runbook hosting
- Escalation ops (pager): ops-pager@redwood.ai - central escalation channel

Meeting cadence and agendas:
- Weekly dependability sync (30 min) - Tuesdays 11:00-11:30 PT
  Agenda: 1) Top 3 signals that changed (5m) 2) Incidents/near misses (10m) 3) Actions & owners (10m) 4) Quick blockers (5m)
- Biweekly SLO alignment review (60 min) - Wednesdays 14:00 PT
  Agenda: metric drift review, canary/rollback triggers, rollout impact analysis
- Shadowing sign-up: managed in a shared spreadsheet; each rotation 48 hours

Measurement plan (what we track):
- Ack latency (P50/P90) for pilot alerts (weekly)
- Number of alert re-routes per week
- Incident count and severity (S1/S2) normalized per 1000 requests
- Ticket churn: postmortem action items reopened within 30 days
- Qualitative feedback: 1-2 sentence survey after shadow windows

Decision triggers (how we decide to scale):
- Green: All experiments meet success metrics and at least 4 product teams volunteer to adopt templates -> scale to org-wide trial for 8 weeks.
- Yellow: Partial success (one or more metrics improved but not threshold) -> iterate experiments + run additional week.
- Red: No measurable improvement or signal increases -> immediate rollback of changes to paging and return to triage-based approach while we investigate root cause.

Risk scenarios and mitigations:
- Risk: Added meeting load causes product teams to opt-out.
  Mitigation: Timebox to 30 min, alternate weekly representation, record notes and require only 1 rep per team.
- Risk: Signal map becomes stale quickly.
  Mitigation: Add a lightweight ownership check to the weekly sync: 'was your map changed this week?' and automate stale checks via a dashboard.
- Risk: Shadowing creates single-point dependency on SREs.
  Mitigation: Limit SRE shadow load to 1 rotation per engineer per month; rotate facilitators; build templates to reduce cognitive load.

Operational runbook sketch (short):
1) For any alert in pilot, first-line responder checks signal map and runbook link.
2) If runbook instructs page X and the owner is not reachable within 10 min, escalation to SRE pool channel.
3) If incident meets S1 criteria, declare bridge and follow incident template in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts).

Next steps (this week):
- Finish signal map template v0.1 (Miguel) - due 2027-02-12 (ENG-4321)
- Invite pilot teams and confirm reps (Priya + Connor) - due 2027-02-13
- Create shared spreadsheet for shadow sign-ups and publish in #dependability (Leah) - due 2027-02-12
- Run kickoff: 2027-02-16 11:00 PT (30 min) - agenda: goals, experiments, owners, immediate blockers

Notes to self / open questions (informal):
- Should we tie any of these signals to cost alerts (Optimize) or keep strictly dependability? Idea: surface cost anomalies but separate cadence.
- How aggressive should automatic reroutes be? Need input from product leads on tolerance for false-positive reroutes.
- Consider lightweight integration with Redwood Console to flag signal map staleness (leverage existing dashboard APIs).

Appendix: quick templates
- Oncall handshake (Slack): "Hi @team, I'm shadowing your oncall this week (YYYY-MM-DD). Please add me to any runbook updates or quick context messages. I'll only step in per agreed rules."
- Signal map columns: signal id | primary owner | secondary owner | runbook link | alert threshold | typical cause | recovery action | last updated
- Short retrospective template: what worked, what didn't, unexpected blockers, metric changes (attach charts)

This doc will be updated after week 2 and week 6 checkpoints with measured results and sample artifacts uploaded to Confluence.

-- Asha
